title: Eurozone inflation at 4% and further ECB rate rises
what_happened: Euro area inflation rose to 3.8% in September 2026 from 3.2% in August, with energy inflation at 18.9%. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% on 2026-10-29. An October reading of 4.0% has been reported but could not yet be confirmed at Eurostat.
how_it_reaches_markets: Higher rates in Europe at the same time as in the US and Japan tighten global financing conditions; pressure on highly indebted euro governments ahead of elections in Spain, France and Italy.

sourced_facts.text: 2026-10-29: the ECB kept its three key rates unchanged: deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing operations 2.65%, marginal lending facility 2.90%
ECB statement of 2026-10-29: 'Inflation rose to 3.8 per cent in September, from 3.2 per cent in August'; energy inflation was 18.9% in September

resolved_when_all: Eurozone headline inflation falls for three consecutive monthly readings
The ECB signals at a policy meeting that it does not expect further rises
worsened_when_any: Eurozone headline inflation reaches 4.5% or more
The ECB raises by more than 0.25 percentage points at one meeting

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: A hike that was fully expected being delivered

history.note: Card opened. Resolution conditions written before the outcome is known.
Sources upgraded in part. The policy decision is taken from the ECB release, read only in part. The Eurostat inflation release could not be opened and the figure stays unconfirmed until it is read.
Second pass. Rate levels and the September inflation figure were confirmed verbatim on the ECB monetary policy statement of 2026-10-29.

Summary rewritten so that it states only what was confirmed at the listed sources and marks the rest as reported. The first version is kept under superseded_sources. Resolution conditions are unchanged.

note: Risk state only. Not a forecast and not investment advice.
unconfirmed_facts: October 2026 euro area inflation 4.0%: Eurostat release titles of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-18 read 'annual inflation up to 4.0%', but the pages could not be opened, so the figure is not counted as confirmed; core 2.6% likewise
Week ending 2026-11-20: STOXX 600 -5.80%, DAX -7.28%: not confirmed at a primary or wire source
A fund manager's expectation of one more ECB hike in December to 2.75%: commentary, not used as support

superseded_sources.reason: Source rule of 2026-11-26: at least one primary source per card; commentary, blogs and reposts are not used as support
facts_as_first_written: October 2026 eurozone inflation 4.0% y/y (from 3.8%); core revised to 2.6% (T. Rowe Price)
Goldman Sachs Asset Management (2026-11-05) expects one more ECB hike in December, to a peak policy rate of 2.75%
Week ending 2026-11-20: STOXX 600 -5.80%, DAX -7.28% (T. Rowe Price)
superseded_sources.summary_as_first_written: Eurozone inflation rose to 4.0% year over year in October 2026 from 3.8%. The ECB is expected to raise rates again in December. European shares had their steepest weekly fall since March in the week ending 2026-11-20.

condition_reading_notes.note: How the conditions above are read. The conditions themselves are unchanged.
notes: Inflation is read from the Eurostat final monthly release. 'Signals that it does not expect further rises' is judged only from the published monetary policy statement: it counts when the statement says rates are at their peak or drops any reference to further increases.
